Brands know use of agents such as Meta Muse is on the rise but are unlikely to hand them the keys to the shop
They promise to find the best Black Friday deals, source Christmas gifts and find the ingredients for a romantic dinner.
This week’s UK launch of the Muse AI assistant by the owner of Facebook and Instagram promises to transform how we shop – and how retailers make money.
Meta has teamed up with high street names including Marks & Spencer, Sainsbury’s, JD Sports and Currys for what the Silicon Valley firm claims is a seamless, secure and time-saving tool.
“From doing the Christmas shopping and searching for a cheaper energy deal, to sorting the school calendar … Muse can get it done for you,” Meta said.
But for companies that have painstakingly transformed from bricks-and-mortar retailers into online emporiums, AI agents pose risks as well as opportunities. Will AI agents kill window shopping, ignore vast online ranges and send shoppers straight to the checkout? Will retailers be forced to discount heavily to stand out? How do they avoid being steamrollered by Silicon Valley tech titans in commercial negotiations?
John Roberts, the founder and chief executive of online electrical goods retailer AO.com, said the impact of AI agents – at present – was “relatively low” but their use as shopping assistants was clearly “a direction of travel”.
He said AO was positioning itself to get recommendations from AI agents in the same way it generally attracted customers, by offering decent prices and good service, which was winning good online reviews on sites such as Trustpilot.
“We need to work out how we are the best option for whichever AI agent you use,” Roberts said.
Working out where to invest is a challenge. Some smaller firms are almost ignoring the developing channel, waiting to see how and where it might go. However, holding back on involvement with the developing technology – such as online shopping in the early noughties – has killed off brands in the past.
Sharon Iles, a senior apparel analyst at the analytics and consultancy firm GlobalData, said those brands that have chosen to partner with Muse would get an early view of how people shop, what they bought through an AI agent and which products got recommended, which could help brands make their listings more visible.
But she said retailers “must continue to prioritise their own channels to protect what an AI agent cannot replace”.
If agents bypass retailers’ websites, said Iles, this could mean companies “miss out on the impulse items that shoppers often add while browsing”, while those selling more complex items such as apparel could find issues with the choice of fit and sizing, “which could lead to higher return rates”.
“Retailers’ own channels should remain the core of their business, and they must give consumers more reasons to shop directly,” she said.
Retailers including Sainsbury’s and Tesco have used their loyalty schemes and websites to build sizeable businesses that monetise customers’ data and sell advertising space to brands.
However, retailers cannot ignore the agents. Muse has proved successful in the US and is ranked first and second respectively on Google and Apple’s free app store, having been downloaded millions of times.
UK residents may be more cautious about agentic technology than those across the Atlantic, but the technology is entering the mainstream. This year, a third of people planning to shop during Black Friday sales intend to get help from AI – up from 19% last year, according to a recent YouGov poll.
To fans, the likes of Muse or rivals such as Google’s Gemini or ChatGPT’s Dots can be a personal secretary helping organise the boring details of life, but to others they are an untenable busybody, parsing their personal data and monetising it.
For Muse to work as Meta envisages, it not only needs access to your email, calendar and shopping apps but details of relationships on apps such as WhatsApp, Facebook and Instagram, your preferences and even your financial and health information.
Sainsbury’s suggests its customers can “tell Muse about their week” and the AI agent will help build a shopping list to provide for dinner parties, different dietary requirements or suggest menus and recipes.
Mark Given, the chief technology and marketing officer at the supermarket chain, said the retailer was “starting carefully, listening to customers” and using what we learn to keep making it better”.
“AI can be genuinely useful, taking on routine tasks like checking offers and building the basket, and helping customers find great value and inspiration more quickly,” he said.
In the UK, Muse must ask for your approval before making a purchase or sending an email, while a separate “security agent” checks the AI tool’s actions against the permissions you have granted.
Meta said Muse had no visibility into people’s passwords or payment methods, and it did not share users’ conversations with advertisers.
However, almost half of shoppers using AI (48%) are concerned about biased or sponsored recommendations, according to YouGov. Rival research firm Kantar found only 23% trusted a chatbot’s recommendations.
Meanwhile, some retailers are territorial about which AI agents get to trawl their data. Amazon has blocked AI agents from its store, although it is reportedly in talks with Meta about allowing access. Last year, Amazon sued the AI company Perplexity over its shopping feature that automates placing orders for users.
Research from the advisory firm KPMG highlights consumer caution. It found just 12% of those planning to shop during Black Friday – a largely online sale event in the UK – intended to use an AI tool (such as prompting ChatGPT or Gemini) specifically to find deals, slightly lower than the 15% using it last year.
Linda Ellett, the head of consumer, retail and leisure at KPMG, said trust would remain an important factor for shoppers and, while some would be happy to give access to their data to “make life easier” and enjoy the ability to “have a chat with an agent” to organise tasks, others would be much more cautious.
With about 70% of shopping still taking place in stores, and more than that in many categories, AI agents have some work to do to kill off the high street.
Brands made familiar through advertising, a store presence or social media content will continue to be important.
Most consumers use AI as only part of their search, to compare prices on kitchen equipment, home electronics or food, for example, or seek recommendations on complicated products such as electronics or supplements.
The advisory firm OC&C said: “For now, AI often helps shoppers validate a choice rather than create an entirely new preference.”
Mark Howell, the director of European retail at Rithum, an e-commerce firm that works with Asos, M&S, Aldi and Shein, said: “Retailers aren’t going to be comfortable handing checkouts entirely to bots until questions around responsibility and liability are resolved.
“Agentic commerce is both real and overhyped. The technology is clearly going to become part of retail, but the legal and commercial realities are much more complicated than people acknowledge. In Europe especially, retailers are asking a simple question: if the bot gets it wrong, who’s liable?”
Retailers and brands said that AI agents were having only a tiny influence on shopping behaviour but most larger businesses already had teams ready to support “generative engine optimisation” (GEO) tactics. These include: making sure they appear in Reddit forums, an important source for some platforms ; ensuring AI models can access correct and more detailed product information in text as well as photographs; and responding to reviews on Google or Trustpilot.
While some have suggested that the use of AI agents could diminish the power of brands and loyalty schemes built up by companies with advertising and paid-for search, Roberts suggested agents might well be influenced by these factors.

texts.https://www.theguardian.com/environment/:
Body urged Bristol city council to reject plan because of risk to nearby protected wildlife and habitats
Natural England objected to the building of a large AI datacentre near Bristol weeks before the government threatened to abolish the independent environmental adviser.
The nature adviser made a significant intervention to urge Bristol city council not to grant planning permission for a 40MW datacentre at Avonmouth, because of the threat to protected wildlife and habitats at one of the UK’s most important sites for migratory birds, which is within 600 metres of the site.
The Environment Agency – which is also threatened with abolition by the de facto deputy prime minister, Louise Haigh – objected in addition to the flooding risk at the site, which is on a high-risk flood plain, expressing concerns people would not be able to take safe refuge in the event of a deluge.
Haigh this week blamed quangos, including Natural England, for blocking development and indicated both bodies could be scrapped with their responsibilities handed to ministers or devolved. Ministers are pushing for the construction of AI datacentres across the country as key to growing the UK economy.
Hundreds of AI datacentres are planned, with more than 300 waiting in the queue to connect to the electricity grid, representing 73GW of demand – almost double the peak winter energy demand for the entire UK. But they face considerable environmental and sustainability issues over their high energy use, pollution, encroachment on protected habitats and emissions from fossil fuel power stations many want to install while waiting for grid connections.
To side-step local democracy, the government is allowing datacentre developers to use the nationally significant infrastructure projects (NSIP) regime, with the secretary of state acting as the decision maker.
But Natural England has expressed concerns to ministers about the rollout of datacentres, urging caution and a precautionary approach.
In a response to the government’s draft datacentre national policy statement , Natural England said AI datacentres were a relatively new development type whose full environmental impacts were still being understood.
It highlighted the potential impact on rare and vulnerable species from overabstraction from waterways to meet datacentres’ demands.
Government sources denied the objection to the datacentre at Avonmouth or Natural England’s stance on taking a precautionary approach to their widespread construction had influenced Haigh’s announcement of their possible abolition.
But Craig Bennett, the chief executive of the Wildlife Trusts, said the government’s threatened abolition of Natural England was a worrying sign of an attack on environmental regulation. “Regulatory arm’s-length bodies like Natural England are set up to implement the law of parliament,” he said. “If we want decisions made about nature on the basis of science rather than the very last private corporate or vested interest that a minister has spoken to, then we have independent arm’s-length bodies like Natural England.”
Earlier this month Natural England advised Bristol city council that the datacentre could cause “disturbance and displacement” to rare and vulnerable bird species within the Severn estuary special protection area, just 600 metres away. Another protected site, Hallen Marsh, was only 270 metres away but had not been accounted for by the developers when assessing noise pollution, Natural England said.
As well as the flood risk, the Environment Agency said the developers had not provided any information on the level of water use, and the risk of pollution from land contamination to controlled waters. More than 4,000 people have objected to the datacentre’s construction.
Bristol council said the proposal was “likely to give rise to significant environmental effects” and it wanted the developers to carry out a full environmental impact assessment.
Mary Stevens, an AI campaigner at Friends of the Earth, said: “Natural England was doing its job brilliantly here as an independent adviser. I would have no confidence if this was a government minister doing the work because they would not be acting independently to protect nature.”
Rivington Energy, which is developing the datacentre, said: “We acknowledge the feedback received from the Environment Agency and Natural England and welcome the opportunity to continue working constructively with all consultees throughout the planning process.
“While substantial environmental and technical assessment work has already been undertaken, additional studies are being prepared in response to comments received and will be submitted as part of the ongoing planning process.
“We … are now preparing a detailed environmental statement to support the next stage of project assessment.”
The Wildlife Trusts have launched a petition to save Natural England, saying the current body and its predecessors have been vital protectors for wildlife, land, water and sea across England since the 1940s.
A government spokesperson said: “Datacentres are essential to our economy, but their development must protect the environment and benefit local communities. Developers must meet planning requirements, with local authorities assessing environmental impacts, and then deciding on local applications.”

There’s just one thing we still don’t know: How much will they cost?
COPENHAGEN, Denmark—If we lived in the world that Volvo’s product planners expected back when the current XC90 debuted in 2015 , both it and the smaller but related XC60 (which arrived in 2017) might have been the last of their kind as everything went electric . As we know, the future hasn’t turned out quite like that, especially in the critically important US market . At the same time, Europe and China are electrifying, which seems like an argument against spending resources on developing all-new replacements for models that might not have an eight-year lifespan in most markets.
So instead, Volvo has given the XC60 and XC90 another lifecycle refresh. The exterior styling tweaks are minimal; the bigger three-row XC90 had already been given a new look last year, and the XC60 now gains a similar grille and the same matrix headlights, for instance. And that’s no bad thing—both were, and remain, handsome shapes that are popular with Volvo’s customer base.
Instead, the Swedish automaker’s attention has been on bringing the technology up to date for model year 2028 standards. Which means a much bigger battery for the PHEVs, with sufficient capacity for a couple of days of daily driving for most of us before needing to be recharged. There’s also new, modern infotainment and interiors that are now even nicer to spend time in than before.
We first saw the revamped 2028 XC60 (and learned about its technical details and those of the XC90) in September , but with the cars going into production now and due to reach the first US customers in the first quarter of next year, we got the opportunity to spend some seat time with the updated cars.
Both the midsize XC60 and three-row XC90 use the same PHEV powertrain. Under the hood, there’s a 2.0 L four-cylinder direct-injection gasoline engine that generates 247 hp (184 kW) and 226 lb-ft (306 Nm) together with a 70 hp (50 kW), 122 ft-lb (165 Nm) electric motor, both of which drive the front wheels. At the rear axle there’s a second electric motor, with an output of 174 hp (130 kW) and 228 lb-ft (309 Nm). Combined output for the hybrid system is 455 hp (339 kW) and 560 lb-ft (759 Nm).
There’s also a much bigger battery, with a net capacity of 37.9 kWh (41.2 kWh gross). If you set the car’s mode to Pure, which relies solely on the rear electric motor for propulsion, that translates to an EPA range estimate of 78 miles (126 km) for the XC60 and 73 miles (116 km) for the larger, draggier XC90. Which is significant—when the average driver drives fewer than 30 miles a day , it means these PHEVs carry enough electrons for a couple of days of tailpipe-emissions-free driving before it needs to be plugged in again or the engine to fire up.
When it is time to plug it back in, expect it to take about four hours with a level 2 charger of at least 16 A, or 27 hours if you’re limited to 120 V. In Hybrid mode, where you get the benefit of both electric motors and the gas engine, Volvo expects a combined efficiency of 67 mpge in the XC60, and 61 mpge for the XC90.
Even if the gas engine is running and you’re in Hybrid or Power mode (which keeps the engine on all the time), you can drive these Volvos as if they were EVs with one-pedal driving: just move the transmission from D to B. The Volvos are always using their electric motors to slow the car before the friction brakes intervene, and in B you get the same amount of lift-off regen regardless of mode. For city traffic, it’s very effective. (In Pure, although only the rear motor deploys energy, both front and rear motors regen brake.)
In power mode, with all 455 hp unleashed, you can chirp the wheels on a wet day, but these model year 2028 cars are about one large male human heavier than the outgoing model year, both of which were already pretty heavy. So don’t expect performance-car performance. The XC60 is the sweeter to drive on a winding road, but both are entirely at home cruising on a highway or creeping along in a city, which is where cars like these spend the vast majority of their time. There’s more road intrusion into the cabin of the XC60—the larger Volvo rides on air suspension that does a much better job of filtering that out.
A first-drive event like this isn’t the best place to get a good read on real-world efficiency. We usually have to share cars with other journalists, and there’s limited time to drive on roads that may not be representative—too sinuous, or not enough traffic, for example. We need to try all the different drive modes and see how cars respond to different inputs. And it’s rare you’ll spend the entire day with one car, finishing at the same point you started.
That said, I can’t give you a definite read on range and efficiency for these two plug-ins. But my unscientific estimate is that my drive partner and I, in an XC60, drove about 60 km in a mix of city driving and higher speeds on the way to Malmo in Sweden, which is on the other side of a gigantic bridge, and we used about half the battery pack to do so. (Volvo asked us to put the PHEVs in Hold or Charge mode at 50 percent to leave some state of charge for whoever drove the cars after lunch.)
Thus, there was little charge left in the XC90 when it was my turn to drive the final stint back into Copenhagen. Since I wasn’t worried about combined efficiency, I ran the car in Charge mode for about 20 min, regenerating the battery from an indicated 10 km to an indicated 21 km, then switched to Pure once we reached the city, with about 16 km to go.
Volvo already had a reputation for great automotive interiors, and with this refresh, it has pushed things forward a little. There’s a new wood finish, new textiles, and new backlighting. The resemblance between the two interiors from the front seat is now quite strong, particularly since the test cars Volvo brought to Denmark wore identical color schemes inside.
Our final 1.6 km to the hotel took more than 30 minutes to negotiate thanks to a reception for very important people that apparently took place next to the hotel. Most of this jam was on one street, with our destination in sight, but the frustration was in part ameliorated by Volvo’s secret weapon: its seat massage function.
Lots of other OEMs offer massaging front seats, which inflate and deflate the internal air bladder to massage your shoulders, back, and sometimes butt. But none massage you with quite the firmness of a Volvo seat. And they have the power to distract you from terrible in-car situations, as I discovered when stuck in a V90 Cross Country with Nigel the Cat, whose way of remonstrating with me about his trip to the feline ophthalmologist was to scream at high volume until he ran out of breath, at which point he’d pant for a few minutes, then start again. The seat in that car is the only reason we both made it home safely. And so, in Copenhagen, I set the seat to pulse and did some box breathing.
As well as new interior materials, you’ll also notice a new infotainment screen in both cars. Gone are the old 9-inch displays, replaced by a new 11.2-inch touchscreen that stands a little proud of the dash rather than recessed into it. Just this one upgrade alone really lifts both interiors; the old, small screen was showing its age. Most Ars readers will recoil at the news that Gemini has replaced the previous Google Assistant , but at least the voice-recognition capabilities are improved. Gemini will still struggle with some commands—I asked it to tell me my current efficiency, which it failed at, but it’s rather good at looking stuff up on the Internet while I drive.
There are also some updated advanced driver-assistance systems, like a warning if cyclists approach your opening door, and an updated 360-degree parking view. But there’s no point-to-point assist like Mercedes is introducing , or a hands-free “level 2+” system like Super Cruise; Volvo’s experience with the EX90 may have left it a little gun-shy.
With a battery…

As artificial intelligence becomes an unavoidable part of everyday life and models become ever more sophisticated, the cost of the energy required to run the technology is ballooning.
To rein in runaway costs, AI labs and cloud providers are trying to build new data centers in places with cheap and plentiful renewable energy— like Scandinavia . But logistical challenges, a scarcity of key components , and a swell of anti-data center protests are getting in the way.
An expanding field of hardware startups, among them German company Q.ANT, is coming at the problem from a different direction: by developing a new breed of chip— photonic processors —meant to minimize the amount of energy that AI models consume.
Whereas regular GPUs transmit and process data by shuffling electrons around, photonic processors use waves of light. Because light doesn’t generate heat as it travels and allows more data to be processed simultaneously, photonic processors supposedly consume less energy and require minimal cooling—one of the largest sources of cost for data centers.
The aim isn’t to replace GPUs with photonic processors, but to run them side-by-side. Whilst GPUs excel at grinding through masses of additions and multiplications—linear math—photonic processors are best suited to complex, nonlinear calculations.
Few photonic processors are running inside data centers today. But Q.ANT recently rolled out its chips to facilities operated by cloud company IONOS as part of a pilot program. It says that more than 30 teams of engineers are now developing AI models optimized for photonic computing.
Earlier this month, WIRED spoke with Michael Förtsch, founder and CEO of Q.ANT. We discussed the energy bottlenecks constraining AI development, how photonic processors differ from regular chips, and the challenges Q.ANT faces in trying to popularize a new class of hardware.
WIRED: Michael, could you start by outlining the problem Q.ANT is aiming to solve? Why does the world need photonic processors to run AI models?
Michael Förtsch: The overall problem is the cost generated by the huge amount of energy consumption.
If you compute the way we think light should be used—not as a direct replacement for a GPU, but as a coprocessor—you basically have a new processor that takes care of the heavy math.
The cost driver today is the access to the memory. The less data you need in order to complete a job, the more efficient and better your system. We execute complicated math in a single step, where [regular chips] need thousands of steps. This saves a bunch of data—or memory access points.
How would you explain to the layperson how photonic computing works? How can light be used to perform mathematical computations?
Light is a wave. What is a wave? A sine function . [ The sine function is a mathematical rule that, when plotted to a graph, produces a smooth repeating wave. —Editor ] If I want to model something that’s round in shape with only linear functions, I need an infinite amount of data points and lines in order to describe something very simple: a circle. If I have the sine function at hand, because light is a wave, I need two points and I have already described the circle in all its beauty.
Light is very, very gifted to operate on complicated equations.
What distinguishes the type of problem best left to regular chips from problems that should be delegated to photonic processors?
The Nvidia H200 GPU is a masterpiece of technology. It’s art. It’s truly hard to attack it in its homeground. But light has strengths where the GPU is weak—and vice versa.
Linear math? Please route it to the GPU. Non-linear and complex stuff? Please route it to us.
We believe we will be much stronger in everything related to pictures and videos: image recognition, segmentation, and generation. Then, everything that’s related to robotics and physical AI.
What is the estimated gain in energy efficiency tied to using photonic processors alongside GPUs for AI tasks?
I’m not saying photonic computing will come for free. But I see that photonic computing, in combination with [CPUs and GPUs], can bring you a lot more artificial intelligence at a fraction of the energy.
Under simulation, we are ending up at around four or five times energy reduction. But in real hardware we are not yet demonstrating it.
Can any task run on photonic hardware by default, or do they need to be configured in a certain way?
There’s no need to learn a different language than C++ or Python. And you can already execute [preexisting] code on our machines.
But if you take something that has been optimized for a GPU only, you should not expect that automatically things will run faster. You have to do some adaptations.
It’s a chicken and egg problem, right? Until developers are building models to run on this type of processor, it’s going to be difficult to sell them to cloud providers. Equally, until photonic processors are available for people to use, it’s going to be tough to convince developers to design for them.
Whether it’s photonic or any other processor technology, it will need time to get the credibility and trust that’s needed for a company like Google to build data center infrastructure around it.
That’s the reason we chose to go into data centers with proof of concept systems, to validate that photonic computing is robust enough to withstand that environment.
We want to invite the world to compute on our systems. We are building a new chicken, so you can start producing eggs. Let’s find out together whether they’re tasty or not.
What else should I understand about why photonic processors are not already widely in use?
If hypothetically we received an order of 100,000 [photonic processors], we at Q.ANT are ready, but I’m not sure about the suppliers.
Hardware is not software. On the assembly side, it will need [time] before we have the same robust supply chain as the semiconductor world.
Do you expect to suffer from the same problem as other hardware challengers in securing capacity with the big chip manufacturers?
[To produce Q.ANT chips] you only need 90 nanometer node technology, from the 2000s. A lot of foundries already use this capability to produce chips that are super cheap. With this technology, you can use the same line to produce high-performance chips with a much higher street price, without massive upfront investment in your assets.
Are Q.ANT processors built to function alongside a particular brand of GPUs—say, Nvidia or AMD—or are they totally agnostic?
There’s no need to go single-sided with a particular GPU. We want to have the freedom to cooperate with any of them.
Either way, we are not competitive to GPUs, we complete their function set.
Can you imagine a future in which AI models run entirely on photonic processors, or will they always be a sidekick?
If we see an opportunity in five years to attack the GPU as well, we would not be shy about taking it. But at the same time, I do not know what workloads in five years are going to be like.
It depends on the architecture of future AI models, you mean?
Could the chance to perform certain calculations more cheaply with photonic processors change the way that AI engineers design future models?
The core message is that we need to do something to fight the energy cost in the AI stack.
That’s where we see the future of AI: very data-optimized models that allow for tasks of the same quality, but at a fraction of the energy—and therefore a fraction of the operating cost.

Platform, yaklaşık 20 yıllık tarihinde ilk kez ebeveynlere çocuklarının hesapları üzerindeki bazı ayarları yönetme imkanı tanıyor. Yeni sistemle birlikte genç kullanıcıların hesapları varsayılan olarak korumalı moda alınacak.
Korumalı mod kapsamında genç kullanıcılar hassas içerikleri görüntüleyemeyecek ve hedefli reklamlarla karşılaşmayacak. Ebeveynler ise çocuklarının platformda geçirdiği haftalık süreyi takip edebilecek, günlük kullanım sınırları belirleyebilecek ve yeni takipçilerin onayını kendi kontrollerine alabilecek. Ayrıca akış önerilerini yalnızca takip edilen hesaplarla sınırlandırabilecek, belirli kelimeleri filtreleyebilecek ve hassas medya içeriklerini kapatabilecek.
Ebeveyn denetimleri, doğrudan mesajlar üzerinde de bazı kontroller sunuyor. Buna göre ebeveynler, çocuklarına kimlerin mesaj gönderebileceğini belirleyebilecek ve çocuklarının kimlerle mesajlaştığını görebilecek. Ancak özel mesajların içeriğine, arama ve görüntüleme geçmişine erişemeyecek. Genç kullanıcılar da hesaplarına getirilen kısıtlamaları görebilecek ve hesaplarının kontrolünü korumaya devam edecek.

Nükleer enerji alanında çalışan Project Omega , 80 milyon dolar yatırım aldı. Şirketin 80 milyon dolarlık A serisi yatırım turuna B Capital liderlik etti. ABD merkezli Project Omega'nın Borusan Ventures’ın da katıldığı yatırım turunda noa VC, 645 Ventures, Starship Ventures, Mantis Ventures ve diğer yatırımcılar yer aldı.
Şirket, yeni gelen yatırımı üretim kapasitesini artırmak ve ilk nükleer yakıt geri dönüşüm tesisinin yapımına başlamak için kullanacağını açıkladı.
Stafford Sheehan tarafından 2025 yılında kurulan Project Omega, kullanılmış nükleer yakıtı yeniden işleyerek enerji üretiminde kullanılabilecek değerli kaynaklara dönüştüren teknolojiler geliştiriyor. Şirket, geleneksel olarak nükleer atık olarak kabul edilen kullanılmış yakıtın içerdiği enerji potansiyelini değerlendirmeyi ve bu kaynağı yeniden ekonomiye kazandırmayı hedefliyor.
Project Omega'nın geliştirdiği erimiş tuz bazlı elektrokimyasal geri dönüşüm teknolojisiyle kullanılmış nükleer yakıttan değerli malzemeleri geri kazanıyor. Saf plütonyum ayrıştırmadan çalışan bu yöntem, nükleer atık hacmini yüzde 90'a kadar azaltma potansiyeli taşıyor. Geri kazanılan malzemeler ise yeniden reaktör yakıtı üretiminde, ticari ve tıbbi amaçlı izotoplarda ve uzun ömürlü güç sistemlerinde kullanılabiliyor.
Şirketin bir diğer çalışma alanı da şarj edilmesi veya batarya değişimi mümkün olmayan koşullarda uzun süreli enerji sağlayan güç sistemleri geliştirmek. Sensörler, otonom sistemler, uzay araçları ve deniz altı platformları gibi kritik görev ekipmanlarına yönelik çözümler üzerinde çalışan şirket, Idaho Ulusal Laboratuvarı ve Pasifik Kuzeybatı Ulusal Laboratuvarı ile de çalışmalar yürütüyor.
Borusan Ventures Kurucusu ve Başkanı Defne Kocabıyık Narter , Project Omega'nın kullanılmış nükleer yakıtı yeniden değerlendirerek bu darboğazı aşmayı hedeflediğini ve farklı reaktör teknolojilerine uyum sağlayabilecek bir iş modeli geliştirdiğini vurguluyor.

The company pretty much invented the hardware superstore when it began in 1978, simply by being so big. It inflated the neighborhood tool shop into a whole city of lumber, hammers, caulk, power saws, and big rolls of wire. I would know I’m in a Home Depot blindfolded because of a distinct quality to the air—crisp and particulate, smelling like wood dust, paint, and the oiled metal of power tools. The Home Depot smell is buried deep in my childhood, filed somewhere between “building a deck” and “first day of spring.” Anyway, the Home Depot website is just as big. And while it doesn’t smell like sawdust, it’s easier to find stuff. Our roundup includes Home Depot promo codes from 20% to $100 off, new customer coupons, free shipping offers, and Pro discounts that can drop prices by as much as 50% when you buy online.
If you register for Home Depot’s Style and Decor newsletter, you receive a special code for 10% off furniture and home accents. Otherwise, you can sign up for the Home Depot coupon newsletter or text alerts to get an immediate $5 off your next in-store purchase of $50 or more. Another easy way to save sitewide at Home Depot is to set up a subscription for your go-to products and automatically get 5% off and free delivery on your order.
If you’re hoping to use this winter to make some much-needed improvements around the house, be sure to take advantage of the major discounts and deals during the Home Depot Black Friday sale . During the sale, you can save hundreds of dollars on home essentials like appliances, tools, furniture, storage, smart home tech, and more.
If you already shop a lot at Home Depot and are looking for other ways to save, signing up for The Home Depot’s Promo Text Program is a good idea. You’ll receive text messages with special promotions, offers, how-to guides for projects, and great design ideas. Plus, you’ll get $5 off your next purchase when you sign up.
And as it turns out, the hardware giant also goes hard on discounts, slashing prices on grills, garden and outdoor power tools, and smokers like the new Traeger Woodridge ( 8/10, WIRED Recommends ), which is also sold at Home Depot .
But that’s not all; Home Depot is covering the whole house! There are appliance deals of up to $1,400 off, $1,000 off washer and dryer sets, and bathroom deals of up to 40% off vanities, 25% off bathtubs, 20% off toilets, and 15% off showers.
Plus, Home Depot has appliance bundle deals where you can get major discounts when you purchase multiple appliances at once.
Home Depot coupons of the moment include whopper deals like 15% off storage solutions and 35% off washers and dryers. Explore more deals on kitchen and other furniture by checking out the deals of the moment here . As we’ve stated, there are so many ways to save at Home Depot, even when you’re shopping online. Special Buy of the Day deals include steep price drops on select products or entire brands—but these significant discounts last only 24 hours. That’s a whole lot of savings for one of the most expensive home renovations you can do. Another savings hack? Jump on products marked with “New Lower Price” to find them at their lowest price yet.
Winter is a great time to stay inside and focus on home improvement projects. Home Depot has everything you need for remodels (including bulk buys). Right now, vinyl plank and tile flooring is up to 30% off, with options starting at 99 cents per square foot. Plus, power tool kit combos can save even more, with bundle deals of up to 70% off—including Deals of the Day flash sales on tools and appliances with rebates of up to $1,000. Deals include smart home items WIRED has covered extensively, like Nest learning thermostats ( 9/10, WIRED Recommends ). Need advice on setting up a smart home? WIRED has your back . Not only do Deals of the Day (and over 1 million products) qualify for free shipping, but you can also get free delivery to your local Home Depot store or straight to your door with online orders over $45.
Home Depot also offers a loyalty program called Pro Xtra for frequent fliers, whether you’re a contractor or just undergoing a serious remodel this year. This means exclusive prices up to 20% off, 10% discounts on bulk buys, a rewards point system, and occasional $50 off $250 coupons. Painting the house? The program also nets you 10 to 20% off paint and primers. Pro Xtra offers multiple tiers, from basic membership to Elite and VIP.
Special Buys of the Week are bargains worth checking out, and pros can get discounts with the Pro Special Buy of the Week —and that’s on top of exclusive coupons, bulk product discounts up to 20% off, and everyday discounted pricing on items. Hot offers this week include: free tools or batteries with your purchase of tools from Milwaukee, RYOBI, and more premium brands, plus 20% off flooring. Also grab 40% off bathroom products like Kohler showers, tubs, vanities, faucets, and toilets, including luxury upgrades like Horow smart toilets and bidets.
Home Depot has long maintained a program offering discounts to active service members, veterans, and their spouses, offering 10% off all eligible purchases. You’ll need to register to verify your military status through SheerID , and from then on, you can just scan your virtual ID or enter your phone number at checkout, the same way you do at the grocery store. Note that military discounts are limited to $400 each calendar year, and this resets each year. Some commodity products are excluded, including lumber, wire, and building materials. Appliances are also out in the cold, but military families may still find special deals or tax-free shopping through Home Depot’s Military Exchange Program.
If you haven’t opened a credit card account at Home Depot , now is a great time. If you have a new account, when you place your first order with your credit card, you can save up to $100 on qualifying purchases.
Plus, you can get up to 24 months of financing on special-order and installed purchases of blinds, shades, and shutters with Home Depot promo code YU8QTSVQ3 . You can also get up to 24 months of financing on installed custom closet purchases with Home Depot coupon code 7MD4H2YQ2 .

If you’re hunting for a new vacuum, Dyson has likely come up in one way or another. The brand is famous for its powerful vacuum cleaners , but its air power also extends to other parts of the home, including hair care and air purification. It’s a dream household staple; I lugged around an old Dyson vacuum for years until I could upgrade to a newer stick model rather than buying something that wouldn’t be as powerful or last as long.
But the cost can make it a hard investment, even if it’s worth it. If you’re shopping for one of Dyson’s long-lasting gadgets but have a limited budget, fear not: we’ve got coupon codes to make it a better buy, plus tips on how to get discounts on Dyson’s website. Read on to get all of our Dyson promo codes and coupons, and learn the best ways to shop for a Dyson.
Dyson is one of the best and most enduring brands of our time. Dyson doesn’t run tons of sales often, so if you’re looking to buy a Dyson product, we have the best ways to save right here. First, be sure to sign up for Dyson’s newsletter to get early access to Dyson’s Black Friday offers and deals. Not only will Dyson have lots of discounts and promotions during the holiday sale, but Dyson will also have deals during the early Dyson Black Friday period in the run-up to Black Friday, for even more opportunities to save. This means savings across all of Dyson’s top tech categories, including hair stylers, hair straighteners, hair dryers, air purifiers, and vacuum cleaners—be sure to keep checking back as more offers are added as the holidays approach.
Usually, you need to be a new customer to get a great discount, but Dyson rewards you for being a repeat customer. You can get 15% off your next order by registering your current Dyson product’s serial number .
You can also get 10 percent off your next Dyson purchase without needing a device to register. You’ll want to sign up your mobile number via a pop-up on Dyson’s homepage . That will send you a text, and you’ll have to reply with “Y” to officially register. After you reply, you’ll receive a message with a link that reveals a single-use code for 10 percent off your next purchase at Dyson.
You can also sign up for texts or Dyson’s email newsletters (like this hair care newsletter) to access exclusive Dyson sale events, more coupon codes, and new product releases (and several new vacuums are due out this year).
Dyson always has sales on its website at the Dyson Deals Hub . The discounts rotate weekly, and there are always different active coupons across different categories of Dyson products. You might find a nice discount on the V12 vacuum , for instance, or on the Dyson Airstrait .
Looking for a bigger discount? Try Dyson’s outlet for refurbished vacuums, hair tools, and air purifiers. You’ll find discounts of up to 30 percent off the original price, and each one is inspected, restored to like-new condition, and backed by Dyson’s official warranty. It’s a good way to get great deals on products like the Supersonic hair dryers, which you can find for under $200 when refurbished, and Dyson’s multi-stylers can be found for under $300. These do have a shorter warranty period than new products, though; it’ll only be six months to a year rather than two to five years.
If you’re looking to invest in this often pricey, long-lasting technology, I’d suggest checking the Dyson deals page, where you can see all the exclusive rotating Dyson offers available right now and shop by category, like cordless vacuums, hair care, air treatment, headphones, and more. Some of the best deals I’ve seen so far include the viral Dyson Airwrap Origin multi-styler and dryer , which has three attachments and is $150 off right now, and the V12 Detect Slim, a highly-rated cordless Dyson vacuum with 60 minutes of run time for $250 off.
Like all of Dyson’s tech lineup, Dyson hair tools have the signature high power, efficiency, sleek design, … and high price tag. One of Dyson’s most iconic and enduring tools is the Dyson Airwrap, which debuted in 2018. We rated it a 9/10 WIRED Recommends for its multifunctionality, offerings for different hair types, less heat use than previous models, and a light, easy-to-use design.
When it comes to hair gadgets, there are many gimmicks that claim to make styling easy and effortless, but the Dyson Airwrap actually works, using air to draw strands of your hair around the curling barrels to produce a lasting result without subjecting your hair to excessive damaging heat. It's a multifunction styler, but the Airwrap really shines as a curling iron. Powered by its internal motor, it creates a vortex of air inside the hollow barrel, powerful enough to draw your hair to it. All you have to do is place the end of your hair near the barrel, and the machine does the gripping and wrapping for you, so you don't have to worry about touching a hot curling barrel.
I’m of the opinion that everyone needs an air purifier and a fan . So why not combine both? (Especially if you are short on space, like me.) We at WIRED love the Dyson Purifier Cool PC2, which works in tandem to cool the air with purified air. Not only does it function as a fan, blowing cool air, but it also captures gases and 99% of pollutants, redistributing cool, purified air throughout your home for a healthier living space. It also conveniently connects to the MyDyson app for hands-free control anywhere, and it’s $200 off right now.
As mentioned above, Dyson has a dedicated deals page , making it easier than ever to find what you’re looking for and save. This includes Dyson’s new OnTrac noise-canceling headphones , now half off at $250. They offer best-in-class noise cancellation, up to 55 hours of battery life, and an ergonomic design for enhanced comfort. Plus, you can mix and match with Dyson’s 360° visualizer before buying to truly customize these noise-canceling headphones .
If you’re looking to invest in this often pricey, long-lasting technology, I’d suggest checking out the Dyson deals page, where you can see all the exclusive rotating Dyson offers available right now and shop by category, such as cordless vacuums, hair care, air treatment, headphones, and more.

Named after NBC’s iconic logo, Peacock is a video streaming service that primarily features series and film content from NBCUniversal studios, as well as news and sports programming. Premium tiers include a larger content library and access to additional NBC Sports, Hallmark Channel, and WWE content—yes, we’re talkin’ wrasslin’. Right now, you can access all those programs with a Peacock Premium subscription. Save up to 50% on your first 12 months with the latest Peacock promo codes for Black Friday and subscription deals.
With over 30 million subscribers and a range of plans, Peacock has quickly become a popular streaming service alongside titans like Netflix and Hulu. It even beat competitors for the Olympics and exclusive Paralympics coverage last summer. With original favorites like The Office, Poker Face, and Brooklyn Nine-Nine , and popular films like Oppenheimer and Jaws (as the film hits its 50th anniversary), there’s something for everyone in the family on Peacock TV. Check out our Peacock coupons, along with other great ways to save while streaming your faves.
With approximately 792 subscriptions, it can be hard to know exactly how much I’m paying for each (not to mention how much I’m spending each month) and which ones have the content I want to watch most. Peacock also knows that most people use several streaming services and that it’s important to choose the ones that fit best with your budget and needs. Coming in clutch when you're still in “stay-inside-and-keep-warm” mode, Peacock is offering one full year of Peacock streaming for only $80.
One of the best ways to save on Peacock streaming is to choose the annual plan instead of the monthly plan. The annual plan costs $80, which means you’ll get 12 months for the price of 10 and save 16% on a Premium yearly plan, for only $9 per month—otherwise it’s $11 when paid monthly. There’s also Premium Plus, which has no ads, the ability to download and watch certain titles while offline, and includes your local NBC channel live, 24/7. This subscription tier is $17 per month, or $14 when paid annually. In short, you’ll be paying only $80 annually for either Basic or Premium plans!
Being a student often means pinching pennies and eating instant ramen—we know you’re trying to save money wherever you can. With this Peacock TV student discount, eligible college students and young adults ages 18 to 24 can get a full year of Peacock Premium for just $6 a month. That’s $8 in savings per month! To claim this Peacock TV student discount, all you need to do is verify your age.
To unlock more discounts on a Peacock subscription, check whether you qualify for their exclusive offers for students, teachers, military members, medical workers, and other first responders. If you want Peacock for the whole family, you can stream on up to 3 devices at once and create up to 6 profiles with kid-safety settings. Peacock also offers discounts for military members and teachers – verify your status to get 12 months of Peacock Premium for $4 per month.
One of the easiest ways to save on streaming services is to bundle them for a major discount. With this Apple TV and Peacock bundle , you get both services together for as little as $15 per month (essentially the price of one). You’ll save over 30% and won’t have to choose between Apple TV and Peacock. The first tier includes Apple TV and Peacock Premium, with movies, TV, Peacock originals, live sports from Peacock, and Apple originals, starting at $15 per month. The next tier, Apple TV and Peacock Premium Plus, includes all of that plus ad-free viewing and downloads, starting at $20 per month. If you already have a Peacock subscription billed directly by Peacock, you can simply sign in and upgrade to the bundle in your account.
If it feels like you’re paying for about 403 streaming services, Peacock has reduced that number by one, at least. Now, you can bundle Xfinity and Peacock and save 40% on all your favorite media content for $15 per month. You can get Peacock, Apple TV+, and Netflix when you add StreamSaver with Xfinity Internet. Prices vary by plan: Netflix with ads is $8 per month, Peacock Premium with ads is $8 per month, and the Peacock Apple TV+ bundle is $15 per month.
There’s also the Xfinity NOW StreamSaver Bundle—for $30 per month, this Xfinity internet bundle includes NOW TV, which offers over 125 live channels and on-demand programming, Netflix with ads, Apple TV+, and Peacock Premium with ads. New or existing Xfinity Internet customers who subscribe to Gigabit or higher speed service can get two years of Peacock Premium for free, to boot! In addition to the above deals, you can get Peacock Premium at no additional cost if you’re a Diamond or Platinum tier Xfinity Rewards member with any level of Xfinity Internet. To redeem, log in to your Xfinity Rewards account, click the "Get Peacock Premium at no extra cost" reward, choose "Get This Reward", and follow the provided steps. You'll receive an email with instructions to activate your offer.
There’s a wide range of new content coming to Peacock this month, including some new releases for reality TV fans like me. Some of the newest content coming to Peacock includes horror-comedy Five Nights at Freddy's 2 , the sequel to the animatronic original nightmare. Plus, rejoice because baseball season is here, and you can catch up on the action by streaming MLB games on Peacock, including Sunday Night Baseball, MLB Sunday Leadoff, and the thrilling Postseason Wild Card Round.
If you’re like me and love to absolutely turn your brain off (I’m talking no neuron flare-ups would be detected in an MRI) and watch reality TV, let me introduce you to the wonderful world of Love Island . If you love watching Instagram models go from room to room, to the pool, to the gym, and back again in a long-form version of a game of Telephone, this is the show for you. The great part is that every episode is about an hour long, and there are approximately 4,200 episodes per season.
If you’re caught up on the latest Love Island drama, get stoked for their newest spin-off, Love Island: Beyond the Villa , where the clueless cast from the latest season tries to attempt the impossible challenge of juggling multiple social media brand endorsements. It’s a real nail-biter.
Beyond beloved reality TV shows and dramas, Peacock truly has something for everyone—especially sports fans. Tons of live games stream on the Peacock app. To watch, log in on your phone, tablet, or streaming device, then navigate to the Sports section to watch your favorite teams.
Basketball season is upon us again, and Peacock is likely the most reliable way to catch all your favorite NBA teams . Basketball fans, you’re in luck: 100 regular-season games are now available on NBC and Peacock, along with NBA playoff games, the Conference Finals, the NBA All-Star Game, and Monday games and Tuesday night doubleheaders throughout the regular season. Note that the basic "Select" subscription tier doesn't include live sports, but Plus and Premium do. Be sure to check the NBA schedule on Peacock and NBC for the full lineup.
If I’m being honest, one of the biggest reasons I have Peacock is its NFL coverage , including Sunday Night Football and playoff games. (Yes, I love Love Island and football; I contain multitudes.) After living across the country, I like to regularly watch the Chiefs, Bills, Niners, Raiders, Lions, and Chargers to keep up with the fandoms I’ve become part of. Trying to find where to watch Sunday Night Football was a headache, but now I can have the big game in my living room. (Now I’m just wondering when technology will catch up and bring Jalen Hurts into my living room as well.) Sports fans rejoice because Peacock often gets exclusive streaming rights to specific games. For example, last NFL season, Peacock was the place to stream the Week 1 game.

Storms brought flooding and strong winds to parts of the United States on Thanksgiving, complicating holiday travel.
Streets were inundated in New Jersey's Sea Isle City and Ocean City, while water spread across parts of Avalon. Borough of Avalon business administrator Scott J. Wahl said the town was seeing some of the worst flooding in its history. A few drivers had to be rescued after driving around barricades and into floodwaters, but no injuries were reported, Wahl said.
At Philadelphia International Airport, aircraft were seen stranded on the tarmac amid the bad weather. The National Weather Service warned of disruption at eastern US airports through Friday morning, citing poor visibility, turbulence, strong winds and ice forming on aircraft.
Wind gusts of 80 km/h or higher were expected along the Interstate 95 corridor. All of New Jersey was under a state of emergency declared by Governor Mikie Sherrill, and parts of New York were under one declared by Governor Kathy Hochul. More than 600,000 homes and businesses were without electricity on Thursday afternoon, mostly in East Coast states, according to the outage tracking website poweroutage.us.
Macy's postponed its 100th Thanksgiving Day Parade in Manhattan until Saturday. It said it acted in an abundance of caution after consulting city officials, amid worries about how the parade's giant balloons would fare in the wind.
Rain and snow also affected the St. Louis area in Missouri, where up to 33 cm of snow was expected. In Wentzville, Missouri, heavy snow partly collapsed the roof of the Wentzville Ice Arena.
On the West Coast, coastal flood warnings were issued from Southern California to the Oregon and Washington coasts because of king tides. These occur when the gravitational pulls of the moon and sun align to raise water levels. A wave tore down part of a pier in Pacifica, California, on Wednesday.
Although both coasts of the US were affected, travel is usually busier in the days leading up to Thanksgiving than on the holiday itself.

Incumbent prime minister Christopher Luxon loses majority and needs support of Opportunity party to remain in power, or country faces another election
The final results of New Zealand’s general election show the incumbent rightwing coalition will need the support of a centrist newcomer party to form a government, and to avoid sending the country back to the polls.
Preliminary results on 7 November handed the National party and its two coalition partners, the populist New Zealand First and libertarian Act parties, a slim two-seat majority, making the election too close to call until final votes were tallied.
On Friday, the electoral commission released the results from nearly 485,000 “special votes” – those cast from overseas or outside a voter’s electorate. National dropped two seats to 40, Labour stayed on 36 seats, the Greens picked up one seat to 17, Act had 13, New Zealand First 12, Opportunity seven and Te Pati Māori five.
The National-led bloc currently has 65 seats. In the 130-seat parliament, 66 seats are needed for a majority.
The revised results mean the National-led coalition has the only realistic path to power – if it can negotiate a deal with Opportunity. If it cannot, New Zealand will probably need to hold another election.
Three electorate seats changed hands after the special votes. Labour won Wairarapa off National with just 81 votes, and took Hamilton East from National with 173 votes. The Greens won Wellington Bays from Labour with 1,610 votes.
If National applies for a recount and wins back just one of those seats, it could return to power with a slim majority and without needing Opportunity. Applications for a recount must be made by 3 December, and results could take another five days.
Special votes in previous elections have favoured the left, and typically have cost the right one or two seats. Until Friday, a question mark hung over whether National would be able to govern comfortably alongside its coalition partners, or whether it would be forced to cut a deal with the Opportunity party – a newcomer centrist party that incumbent prime minister Christopher Luxon had previously ruled out working with.
After the election, Luxon softened his stance on his initial rule-out, saying he intended to find common ground with the Opportunity party.
On Friday afternoon, Luxon said National will now begin formal negotiations with New Zealand First, Act and Opportunity, but he cautioned discussions would be “challenging” and could take some time.
“Getting it right matters far more than getting it done quickly,” Luxon said. “Kiwis won’t thank us for rushing to an agreement that falls apart, or for sending them back to the polls.”
Lara Greaves, a political scientist at Victoria University of Wellington, said the prospect of New Zealand heading back to the polls was unprecedented, because negotiations between the four parties will be so complex.
“It’s not a 0% chance, it’s the highest chance we’ve ever had of it being another election,” she said.
Opportunity, led by Auckland businesswoman Qiulae Wong , has long said it will negotiate first with the party that secures the highest number of seats.
After the final results were announced, Wong confirmed she would speak with Luxon and that her party’s bottom-lines – which include climate and environment policies and capping political donations – were non-negotiable.
The party would focus on bringing New Zealanders a stable government, Wong told media, and she did not rule out heading back to the polls.
“Clearly stability is important. But setting that more hopeful and aspirational vision, where we can come together as much as possible as New Zealanders and move forward, I think is the priority,” she said.
Having Opportunity in parliament was a “pivotal moment” for the country, Wong said.
“I have every expectation that we will get in there and we will deliver, regardless of what shape the government takes.”
Previously, Wong has said its vision for a low-emissions future, and an inclusive New Zealand, will drive its final decision . Its five bottom-line issues include action on New Zealand’s supermarket duopoly, capping political donations, a 10-year cross-party plan for health, ending bottom trawling in the fishing industry and strengthening New Zealand’s climate commitments.
Negotiations with Opportunity could hit a snag with National’s coalition partner New Zealand First. On Friday, Wong confirmed she would not strike a deal if New Zealand First’s leader, the veteran politician Winston Peters, serves as foreign affairs minister – a position he has held on three occasions.
“We think that his behaviour over successive governments is not the kind of behavior that we expect of someone in that position,” she said.
In other points of tension, New Zealand First and Act have diametrically opposed climate policies, and Act are also unlikely to back Opportunity’s drive for political donation reforms.
Greaves said the Opportunity party will have to make difficult decisions over what it is prepared to gain, or lose. “For minor parties, it’s really hard to go into coalition, or be seen as being too close to a major party or propping up a government, and then turn around later and sell their brand ... as separate from that [major] party.”
Labour leader Chris Hipkins said he was proud the party had gained the highest share of the party vote, but was disappointed it could not deliver a change of government.
It is the second election Hipkins has lost, raising questions over his political future. Hipkins said a decision over his leadership would be made after a government had been formed.
New Zealand could be facing weeks of negotiations in what could become its first ever four-party coalition. In 2023, negotiations took five weeks. With Christmas just four weeks away, New Zealand may need to wait until 2027 to know the shape of its next government.

Powerful storms threaten Thanksgiving travel across North America
A massive Thanksgiving storm hammering the Midwest and north-east with heavy rain and winds, along with high tides out west, is causing widespread disruptions across the US.
More than 80 million Americans expected to be travelling this week. On Thursday 460 flights in the US were cancelled and another 2,508 flights into, out of, or within the US were delayed, tracking site FlightAware said.
The FAA has previously warned that delays would be possible "throughout the week" as a result of the rain and wind that are forecast.
Meanwhile, almost one million households were without power on Thursday night, with Pennsylvania, Maryland and Virginia the hardest hit states.
FedEx aircraft sends dirt flying while overshooting Miami runway
On Thursday, a powerful storm hit the eastern US, bringing damaging winds of up to 70mph, torrential rain, and major coastal flooding.
New Jersey Governor Mikie Sherrill declared a state of emergency as several communities along the Jersey Shore saw widespread flooding.
New York Governor Kathy Hochul also declared a state of emergency for New York City, Long Island and Westchester County.
In New York City, organisers of the annual Macy's Thanksgiving parade have postponed the event to Saturday.
Bridges closed in Maryland due to severe winds and waves battered beaches in Delaware as water seeped onto the boardwalk.
In Maryland, almost two million customers have been asked by the water utility to use water for essential use only due to "intermittent power disruptions".
On the wettest Thanksgiving on record in Washington DC, tidal waters surged and soaked runways at Reagan Washington National Airport, according to the National Water Prediction Service.
More than 980,000 households were reporting power outages by Thursday evening, with Pennsylvania, Virginia, Maryland and New Jersey hit particularly hard.
Pennsylvania Governor Josh Shapiro said that utility providers were working tirelessly to restore power. Meanwhile, energy companies in Virginia and New Jersey warned it may take some time, even days, for power to return, as crews had to wait until it was safe to access damaged areas.
On Thursday afternoon, President Donald Trump said he would consider releasing emergency funds for the east coast as it faces down the holiday storm.
Across the US, severe weather is also descending on the West Coast. The NWS has warned of a series of Pacific storms that are expected to bring rain, mountain snow and strong winds.
Many are bracing for potential flooding as king tides peak along the coast.
Water levels along California's vast coastline could reach over 8ft (2.4 metres) in some areas on Thursday, according to the NWS, breaking records set just last month.
Both San Diego and Los Angeles reported a high tide of over 8ft earlier in the week, and beach-goers were advised to avoid coastal areas.
Train services along the Amtrak Pacific Surfliner, which runs along the California coastline, cancelled several trains due to "washout conditions from high tides", the company shared on social media.
Storms are also forecast for the Pacific Northwest, including the Canadian province of British Columbia.
High king tides threaten California coastline, flood communities
In Miami, some travel delays persisted into Thursday after a FedEx plane overshot the runway the night before, which prompted the closure of all but one runway at the airport for a brief period.
A statement FedEx provided to US media confirmed that one of its flights had "experienced an issue upon landing".
It added: "We are grateful that our crew is safe and there are no reported injuries. We are coordinating closely with investigating authorities, and any additional questions should be referred to the FAA."
An airport employee who spoke anonymously to CBS News, the BBC's US partner, raised the possibility that rainy conditions had been a factor.

If the ruling bloc cannot reach a deal, the country may have to go back to the polls
New Zealand's ruling coalition has fallen short of a parliamentary majority by one seat, following a campaign shaped by a sluggish economy and disillusioned voters.
It now needs the support of the centrist Opportunity Party to remain in power. If they cannot reach a deal, the country may have to go back to the polls.
The incumbent National Party led by Prime Minister Christopher Luxon secured 40 out of 130 seats, while its coalition partners ACT and New Zealand First took 13 and 12 respectively.
A government led by the centre-left Labour Party is not possible, official results on Friday show, as the bloc would not have enough seats even if Opportunity threw its weight behind it.
Luxon on Friday acknowledged that negotiations "may be challenging" and will take some time.
"Kiwis won't thank us for rushing to an agreement that falls apart or for sending them back to the polls," he told reporters.
Labour leader Chris Hipkins said his party "ran an incredible campaign" but acknowledged that it doesn't have negotiating power despite winning the popular vote. "More New Zealanders voted for change at this election than for the status quo," he said.
New Zealand's mixed-member proportional voting system means most governments are coalitions. Each person casts two votes – one for their preferred political party and another for their choice of local representative.
Labour secured 36 seats, The Greens took 17, while Te Pāti Māori, which represents Māori interests, picked up five.
Opportunity, which has been described as this election's kingmaker, secured seven seats. Opportunity's leader Qiulae Wong told reporters her party will negotiate with National, but that all options remain on the table.
"There are seven parties in parliment and everyone is responsible for making sure we do everything we can to deliver a stable government for New Zealand. It's not just up to us," she said on Friday.
Preliminary results on 7 November, election day, had projected that National combined with its coalition partners would have a slim lead over the left-leaning bloc.
But today's official tally shows it had lost two seats on special votes - cast by citizens who were overseas or outside of their registered electorate on election day - which typically skew left.
Some of National's key election pledges include lower taxes, cheaper energy, more renewable generation, and a greater focus on defence.
Labour, meanwhile, had campaigned to cut healthcare, public transport and fuel costs, more government support for social housing, among other things.
In earlier interviews with the BBC, many voters had expressed frustration over spiralling costs of living and high unemployment across the country, with declining faith in their political leadership.
"There's this kind of apathy and a bit of dread," said 21-year-old Imogen Vlutger.
A 40-year-old man said he didn't vote as he could not bring himself to tick any of the boxes on the ballot paper.
More than half of the country no longer see New Zealand as a land of opportunity, according to a survey by the Helen Clark Foundation, a public policy think tank.
Kiwis have been leaving the country in record numbers, with many of them, including former prime minister Jacinda Arden , moving to Australia.

Volodymyr Zelensky has voiced deep frustration with the US, criticising Donald Trump for calling Vladimir Putin "my friend" and saying delays in delivering vital anti-ballistic missiles were costing Ukrainian lives.
In an interview with the BBC at his central Kyiv office, Ukraine's president complained the US was not pushing Russia hard enough in peace talks, and called it "strange" that Trump posted a photo of himself embracing Putin.
"Of course it's up to the President of the United States, but... it's strange," Zelensky said, speaking in English.
"He's an aggressor, and a killer…He can't be a friend. Just cannot be," he said, adding it was like saying you were friends with Adolf Hitler during World War Two.
Since a bruising encounter with Trump in the Oval Office in 2025, Zelensky has been careful how he handles relations with the United States.
Trump's two envoys have been trying to negotiate a peace deal between Russia and Ukraine - to end the huge loss of life. But they often seem more in tune with Moscow's position, than that of Kyiv.
The latest round of peace talks, mediated in Abu Dhabi earlier this month, made no obvious progress: "The more we know, the more problems", is how Zelensky described it.
On Thursday, Donald Trump posted on his Truth Social platform that at his own summit with Putin in China last week he had urged Russia to "pull back all military aggression against territories throughout Europe" and said he believed a peace deal with Ukraine was "a strong possibility".
But from its public statements, Russia appears to have regressed to its initial, hardline negotiating positions – on everything.
And Zelensky revealed that it was not clear whether European negotiators would be at the table, as the US envoys had announced .
Europe ready for talks with Russia on ending war in Ukraine, leaders say
Zelensky says Putin is a 'killer' after Trump calls Russian leader a friend
Ukraine urgently needs the talks to move forward and bring five exhausting years of Russia's full-scale invasion to an end.
Russian strikes across the country have been growing more frequent and more deadly: the number of civilians being killed is at an all-time high.
So Zelensky called for "real helpful allies, who can push Russia" to achieve results and urged the US to live up to its reputation as a strong country with "power and respect".
"When you try to be very neutral with the aggressor... it means you support victims and you support also aggressor. It's not right," he said.
The US argues that it is neutral: in the complex search for a peace deal between the two sides that can hold.
The air alerts, day and night, are now a draining feature of everyday life. As Russian ballistic missiles target power stations and bridges, jet-powered drones are launched daily at central Kyiv and other big cities.
Ukraine launches hundreds of drones at targets in Russia in response.
Zelensky said the military here are now able to destroy about 70% of Russia's fastest drones, a statistic he said was improving.
But there is a "very, very big" deficit of interceptors to stop ballistic missiles and he said the Americans were delaying deliveries of its Patriot systems.
"It's a pity they made a focus on Middle East and they help them more… It's a pity. We have huge questions with this," Zelensky said.
He also confirmed that the US satellite communications system, Starlink – and its military version, Starshield – were still being restricted in occupied areas of Ukraine.
Ukrainian drone units have described their problems to the BBC, as their interceptor drones can no longer catch up with Russian Shaheds. It means those weapons then fly deeper into Ukraine, unhindered.
"Technically SpaceX, politically - I don't know, I really don't know," Zelensky replied. "It's like... ping pong. We are asking one side, they say it's the other."
Ukraine's own long-range strikes against Russian targets have increased in recent weeks, including oil refineries and ships carrying weapons or fuel.
On Thursday, Italy's Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni said an attack that sank a Russian warship docked in eastern Libya this week risked spreading war to the Mediterranean, which was unacceptable.
Zelensky defended the move, calling the warship Merkury an "absolutely fair goal".
He accepted that such strikes were "very dangerous" but said Ukraine's forces "never attack" without co-ordinating with its partners.
But he acknowledged that Ukraine was bracing for a difficult and dangerous winter.
Recent attacks on Kyiv have targeted bridges over the vast river Dnipro, apparently trying to cut the city in two.
Some residents have already left town for the winter and businesses closed, as power cuts and strikes on logistics networks have pushed operating costs unmanageably high.
"People can go, but we will try to defend our capital in any way. We need our capital. Without a capital, you don't have a country."

The final results of New Zealand’s November 7 election offer no clear path to forming a government, suggesting tricky political wrangling is likely in the weeks ahead.
The results, released on Friday, showed that the ruling centre-right coalition led by Prime Minister Christopher Luxon’s conservative National Party has fallen one seat short of a parliamentary majority.

Taiwanese officials raise alarm over interference by China in elections that will shape fortunes of ruling party
Taiwanese voters go to the polls on Saturday in closely watched local elections that will shape the fortunes of the ruling Democratic Progressive party (DPP) as it navigates an increasingly precarious set of relationships on the global stage.
Saturday’s vote will choose mayors, council members and other local leaders across 22 districts. Unlike the presidential elections, in which foreign policy is often a key issue, the local elections, held every four years , are largely focused on bread-and-butter issues such as housing affordability and wealth distribution.
Nevertheless, China looms large over the vote, which takes place against the background of intense military pressure from Beijing . China claims Taiwan as part of its territory despite never having ruled the self-governing island. Taiwanese officials have raised the alarm over thousands of incidents of suspected misinformation or election interference, and certain candidates have been subjected to harassment from the Chinese authorities. There have also been reports of hundreds of China-linked AI-generated videos spreading disinformation about Taiwanese politicians disliked by Beijing.
Beijing calls the allegations of election interference “completely fabricated”. Zhu Fenglian, a spokesperson for China’s Taiwan affairs office, said the allegations “stir up anti-China sentiment to win votes”.
Wei-Ting Yen, a political scientist at Academia Sinica, Taiwan’s national research academy, said: “Even though local elections are not about China, the outcome of local elections will have huge implications for cross-strait relations.”
Most races are a tight competition between a candidate from the ruling DPP and the main opposition party, the Kuomintang (KMT). The KMT promotes closer ties with Beijing, and its chair, Cheng Li-wun, travelled to China this year to meet Xi Jinping, China’s leader. Xi has vowed to unify China with Taiwan, and has not ruled out using military action to achieve that aim.
Yen said if the KMT loses some of its traditional strongholds, Beijing “may need to reconsider what is the most effective strategy for influencing Taiwanese people”.
One of the most contentious votes is the race for Taipei mayor, an office that has been held by the KMT for three decades. The DPP has selected as its challenger Puma Shen, a national legislator whom Beijing declared a “diehard separatist” in 2024. It is the first time a candidate under sanctions by Beijing has run to be mayor of Taiwan’s capital city. In the neighbouring New Tapei City race, the DPP’s Su Chiao-hui is also proving to be a ferocious challenger to the incumbent KMT.
Shen said in a recent interview that even if he didn’t win, the capital’s mayoral race was “a slap to China” because it proved that “democracy works here in Taiwan”.
Huang Bo-kai, a 23-year-old law student, said his top concern was cross-strait relations and how US-China relations were evolving. “The world’s three major powers are increasingly willing to flex their muscles: the US attacking Iran, Russia attacking Ukraine. I think Taiwan could very well be the next target [of China],” he told the Guardian.
Taiwan’s president, the DPP’s Lai Ching-te, is detested by Beijing and has taken a bolshier stance on cross-strait relations than his predecessor, Tsai Ing-wen, who was admired for her ability to drum up support in Washington while walking a delicate tightrope to avoid angering China.
Lai has pushed for greater spending on weapons to deter military aggression from China. The government has proposed a record 18% increase in defence spending for next year, including for drones and missiles, taking it above 1tn Taiwan dollars (£23bn) for the first time.
But many Taiwanese voters would rather that money was spent on more immediate economic issues. Lev Nachman, a political scientist at National Taiwan University, said the national leaders of the DPP and KMT had been notably absent from the mayoral races, reflecting the extent to which campaigns were focused on local issues.
Going into the campaigns for the 2028 presidential elections, Lai would “try to take advantage of the momentum that [Shen] and Su have built for the DPP,” Nachman said, noting that support for those candidates would not necessarily translate into support for Lai.
Tony Yeh, a Taipei man in his 70s, said: “To put it simply, the authorities should do more to boost the economy and buy fewer weapons.”
Taiwan’s economy has boomed this year, largely thanks to the pivotal role that its semiconductor industry plays in the global artificial intelligence rally. The economy grew by more than 14% in the first nine months of the year, the fastest rate in 50 years. But nearly 70% of workers earned less than the average monthly wage of 49,152 Taiwan dollars (£1,137) in the same period.
Yeh said: “Most traditional industries are having a really tough time.”
William Yang, a senior analyst at the International Crisis Group, said: “The issues that really are going to determine their votes are livelihood issues including the stagnant wage, the astronomically high housing price, the affordability issue, and how the government can better make sure Taiwan’s incredible economic boom fuelled by the global AI growth is going to be distributed more evenly.”
Other voters have more niche concerns. Walking her dog in a park, Kuo Wei-tong, a nail salon worker, said policies affecting pets were among her top concerns.
“People are having fewer children and getting more cats and dogs,” she said. “I think that’s something worth giving serious consideration to as well.”
